Grammar is fine. Facts are usually fine.

excerpt_i18n.en:
For a long time, climate, weather, and Earth system research have relied almost entirely on numerical simulations. Supercomputers are tasked with solving physical equations layer by layer, where the precision, resolution, and stability of the models determine how much humans can "see" into natural systems. In recent years, with changes in computing power, artificial intelligence has increasingly been introduced into these traditional fields. Particularly in climate and Earth system modeling, AI is held with high expectations: can it fill in the details that numerical models struggle to cover? Can it provide a finer view of the system under limited computing power? These questions are becoming unavoidable discussions in the fields of supercomputing and scientific computing.

Earth system models represent one of the most typical scenarios in this regard. From global circulation to local weather, from oceans to the atmosphere, and from kilometer-scale to finer variations, the processes these models need to handle are extremely complex and nearly impossible to fully exhaust. Precisely because of this, academia and engineering circles have maintained a cautious, even divided, attitude toward how AI should be integrated into Earth system modeling.

At the GAIR 2025 conference, discussions on the relationship between artificial intelligence and scientific computing were once again brought into focus. Professor Fu Haohuan shared insights during the event, exploring the boundaries and possibilities between numerical simulations and AI in the context of Earth system models and supercomputing practices. As a professor at the Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School and deputy director of the National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen, he has long been engaged in both areas.

Las supercomputadoras se encargaban de procesar ecuaciones físicas capa por capa, donde la precisión, resolución y estabilidad de los modelos determinaban cuánto podía "ver" la humanidad en los sistemas naturales. excerpt_i18n.en: For cloud providers, breaking through is now an urgent imperative. After years of fierce market competition, the cloud market has become suffocatingly constrained—relentless price wars, projects resistant to standardization, and high-investment business models difficult to scale have trapped providers in a quagmire. Could large models, repeatedly hyped by the market, be the breakthrough for cloud providers to escape this mire? Many believe so, but the path forward remains unclear. On December 18–19, ByteDance’s Volcano Engine held its 2025 Winter Force conference, showcasing new advancements like the Doubao large model 1.8 and the video generation model Seedance 1.5 pro, aiming to carve a "channel" through the industry’s rigid barriers and channel the "living water" of AI into the sector. It can be said that Agent represents today’s "super consensus" for AI breakthroughs, but how to develop Agents remains a "diverse narrative" with varied opinions among providers. The Agent Infra platform—"AgentKit"—is Volcano’s answer to this "major test." While there are many Agent developer platforms today, what is the logic behind Volcano’s development of AgentKit? Clues may have long been hidden in the history of Volcano Engine’s evolution. Volcano’s MaaS reaching the top spot is largely due to seizing the AI dividend. In 2025, which cloud provider’s MaaS is leading the way? The answer is undoubtedly Volcano Engine.
excerpt_i18n.es: La necesidad de que los proveedores de servicios en la nube busquen una salida es hoy más urgente que nunca. Los grandes modelos, repetidamente promocionados y sobrecalentados por el mercado, ¿podrían ser la clave para que los proveedores de nube escapen de este atolladero? Muchos así lo creen, pero la forma de lograrlo aún no está clara. On December 23, the globally authoritative AI benchmark platform Artificial Analysis released its latest image model rankings. Alibaba's 6B-parameter Z-Image Turbo surpassed the 32B FLUX.2 to become the strongest open-source image generation model. Currently, the model is available on Alibaba Cloud's Bailian platform, costing only $5 to generate 1,000 images.

Alibaba's Z-Image Turbo overtook FLUX.2 to top the Artificial Analysis image model rankings. According to official data from Artificial Analysis, Z-Image Turbo achieved an ELO score of 1152, setting a new record on the leaderboard. Industry experts consider it one of the best-performing, fastest-generating, and most affordable image generation models available.

Z-Image Turbo supports deployment on consumer-grade graphics cards with 16GB of VRAM. In an H100 deployment environment, it takes only one second to generate images comparable to those produced by models with tens of billions of parameters. In terms of output quality, the model significantly enhances the realism of images, finely restoring details such as skin texture, hair strands, and fabric materials. It also improves bilingual text rendering capabilities in Chinese and English, maintaining clear text and natural layouts even in challenging scenarios like small fonts, complex typography, or poster designs.

Z-Image Turbo can generate hyper-realistic images and bilingual Chinese-English posters.

As a benchmark event in the AI industry-academia-research-investment community, GAIR has consistently adhered to the core principle of "heritage + innovation" since its inception in 2016, dedicated to bridging cutting-edge technology with industrial practice. Li Dongdong (Moderator): Founding Partner of Sanfeng Investment  
Shi Tianhui: Co-founder and Product Vice President of Qingcheng Jizhi  
Xu Yongchang: CIO of Langte Intelligent AI Division (Langqing Shuke)  

"Shifting from helping clients save money to helping them earn money is key to the commercial loop in the computing power industry. Our understanding of the commercial loop is that the circulation efficiency of many computing power cards in China is low, and data center vacancy rates are high. Therefore, we invested in Beijing Lijiu Technology, focusing on the recycling of computing power cards, with the core aim of helping clients drastically reduce procurement and hardware costs—a form of cost-saving." —Li Dongdong

excerpt_i18n.es: Los días 12 y 13 de diciembre de 2025, se inauguró oficialmente la octava Conferencia Global de Inteligencia Artificial y Robótica (GAIR) en el Sheraton Shenzhen Bo'Lin Tianrui Hotel. Como evento referente en el ámbito de la investigación, educación, industria e inversión en IA, GAIR, desde su fundación en 2016, ha mantenido el núcleo de "herencia + innovación" y se ha dedicado a conectar la vanguardia tecnológica con la práctica industrial. En la sesión especial "La Nueva Década de la Capacidad de Cálculo de IA" del día 13, durante el diálogo de mesa redonda titulado "¿Cómo pasar de la 'infraestructura de capacidad de cálculo' al 'ciclo cerrado de valor'?", varios expertos veteranos del sector llevaron a cabo un fascinante intercambio y una profunda discusión, planteando numerosas perspectivas altamente inspiradoras. excerpt_i18n.en: On December 12-13, 2025, the 8th GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit officially commenced at the Sheraton Shenzhen Bo'Lin Tianrui Hotel. As a benchmark event in the AI industry-academia-research-investment community, GAIR has consistently adhered to the core principle of "heritage + innovation" since its inception in 2016, dedicated to bridging cutting-edge technology with industrial practice. As artificial intelligence increasingly becomes a core variable in national competition, computing power is reshaping technological pathways and industrial structures at an unprecedented pace. The "AI Computing Power: The Next Decade" session held on the 13th focused on computing power—the foundational core of intelligent systems—engaging in systematic discussions from architectural evolution and ecosystem development to industrial implementation, aiming to clarify key variables and development directions for China's AI industry over the next decade. At the GAIR 2025 "AI Computing Power: The Next Decade" session, Mr. Lü Haifeng, Co-founder of Dingxi Zhi Chuang, shared insights on "Scientific Intelligence-Driven New Material Design and R&D." As "AI for Science" transitions from concept to industrialization, new material R&D is regarded as one of the most promising application scenarios. However, behind abundant computing power and high expectations, a real barrier is becoming increasingly clear: high-quality, high-value specialized data, rather than computing power itself, is emerging as the key bottleneck hindering AI-driven material discovery from experimentation to mass production. Lü Haifeng's practice stems from directly confronting and overcoming this bottleneck. He has personally witnessed the entire journey of China's supercomputing, from its beginnings at the tera-scale, through service-oriented exploration, to industrial application.
excerpt_i18n.es: Los días 12 y 13 de diciembre de 2025, se inauguró oficialmente la octava edición de la Conferencia Global de Inteligencia Artificial y Robótica (GAIR) en el Sheraton Shenzhen Boao Tianrui Hotel. Como evento de referencia en el ámbito de la investigación, la educación, la industria y la inversión en IA, GAIR, desde su creación en 2016, ha mantenido el núcleo de "herencia + innovación" y se ha dedicado a conectar la vanguardia tecnológica con la práctica industrial. En un momento en que la inteligencia artificial se está convirtiendo gradualmente en una variable central en la competencia entre naciones, la potencia de cálculo está remodelando las rutas tecnológicas y las estructuras industriales a una velocidad sin precedentes. La sesión especial "La Nueva Década de la Potencia de Cálculo en IA", celebrada el día 13, se centró en la potencia de cálculo, núcleo fundamental de los sistemas inteligentes, abordando sistemáticamente desde la evolución de la arquitectura y la construcción del ecosistema hasta la implementación industrial.

excerpt_i18n.en: On December 18, the Volcano Engine Force Conference at the Shanghai World Expo Center was packed with attendees. Tan Dai stated that as of December this year, the daily token usage of the Doubao large model has exceeded 50 trillion, ranking first in China and third globally. Over 100 enterprises have accumulated token usage exceeding one trillion on Volcano Engine. The conference unveiled a series of models, including the Doubao large model 1.8 and the Doubao video generation model Seedance 1.5 pro, which, as always, lived up to the expectations of the audience. As a latecomer in the cloud computing field, Volcano Engine is riding the wave of large models to become a force to be reckoned with in the industry. What has Volcano Engine done right to achieve this? In the era of AI cloud, token usage is becoming a core metric. Two years into the surge of large models, MaaS is emerging as a key battleground for cloud providers and a new infrastructure. Tokens have become a crucial measure for evaluating the industrial implementation of large models. At the Force Conference, Tan Dai candidly remarked, "At every Force Conference, we announce the daily token data of the Doubao large model. This is because a model only delivers value when it is called upon, and the more valuable the model, the more frequently it is invoked." Token consumption often accurately reflects the actual usage during the product implementation process of enterprises. In other words, in the MaaS era, token consumption better indicates a cloud provider's market share. In the past, discussions about cloud computing typically revolved around IaaS and PaaS.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 18 de diciembre, el Centro de Exposiciones de Shanghai estaba abarrotado durante la conferencia de Fuerza Motriz de Volcano Engine. Los modelos presentados en la conferencia, como Doubao 1.8 y el modelo de generación de vídeo Seedance 1.5 pro, cumplieron una vez más con las expectativas del público. Como recién llegado en el campo de la computación en la nube, Volcano Engine está aprovechando el impulso de los grandes modelos para convertirse en un actor ineludible en la industria. items.raw_excerpt: 随着大语言模型逐渐走向真实应用，推理阶段的性能问题正在成为制约落地的关键因素。 模型规模不断增大、上下文持续拉长，再加上 RAG、MoE 等新用法的引入，使得延迟、吞吐和能耗不再只是“调一调参数”的问题，而是直接影响系统架构和算力成本的核心挑战。 围绕这些问题，来自中国科学院计算所的严明玉团队，联合中国电信云计算研究院、浙江实验室和北京大学的研究者，在论文《A Systematic Characterization of LLM Inference on GPUs》中，对大语言模型在 GPU 上的推理行为进行了系统研究。 不同于以往侧重单一模型、单一算子或局部优化的研究路径，严明玉团队从系统和硬件协同的视角出发，通过大规模实验，对大语言模型在 GPU 上的推理行为进行了全面刻画，试图从根本上回答一个长期困扰工程实践的问题：大模型推理为什么会呈现出现在这样的性能特征。 这项工作并没有直接给出如何优化的现成答案，而是首先建立了一套统一、可解释的性能认知框架，将 Prefill 与 Decode 的差异上升为系统级的基本规律，并在不同模型规模、不同硬件平台以及 MoE、RAG 等新型推理范式下进行了验证。 在这一框架下，推理延迟、资源利用率和能耗不再是孤立的指标，而是随着工作负载和系统配置发生有规律的变化。这种从现象出发、最终回到系统根因的研究方式，使得这项工作更像是在为大模型推理建立一张可理解、可推演的性能全景图，而不是提供某个场景下的经验结论。 论文链接：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.01644v1 一次对大模型推理性能的系统性拆解 严明玉团队的这项工作通过大量有组织的实验，系统地总结了大语言模型在推理阶段的性能规律，而不是停留在零散的经验观察上。研究团队发现，LLM 的推理过程在本质上可以分成两个完全不同的阶段，而且这种差异并不是靠优化就能消除的。

excerpt_i18n.en: As large language models gradually move toward real-world applications, performance issues during the inference stage are becoming a critical factor limiting their deployment. The continuous increase in model scale, the ongoing extension of context length, and the introduction of new usage patterns such as RAG and MoE have turned latency, throughput, and energy consumption from mere "parameter tuning" issues into core challenges that directly impact system architecture and computational cost. Addressing these issues, a team led by Yan Mingyu from the Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with researchers from China Telecom Cloud Computing Research Institute, Zhejiang Lab, and Peking University, conducted a systematic study of LLM inference behavior on GPUs in their paper "A Systematic Characterization of LLM Inference on GPUs." Unlike previous research that focused on single models, single operators, or localized optimizations, Yan Mingyu's team adopted a system-hardware co-design perspective. Through large-scale experiments, they comprehensively characterized LLM inference behavior on GPUs, aiming to fundamentally answer a long-standing question in engineering practice: why does large model inference exhibit its current performance characteristics? This work does not directly provide ready-made answers on how to optimize but first establishes a unified, interpretable performance cognition framework. It elevates the differences between Prefill and Decode to a system-level fundamental principle and explores these across varying model scales, different hardware platforms, and novel inference paradigms such as MoE and RAG.
